units.translation: 751-53a. But not at all Medea: the word μάλα is redundant. The sense in order: but sweet sleep did not at all seize Medea, who feared the mighty strength of the bulls.
b. By longing for the son of Aeson: he has not correctly used 'longing' instead of 'love'. For longing is the seeking, but love is an intensified passion.
2 Ptolemy, On the Distinction of Words (Herm. 22, 1887, 410, 12); Ammonius, On the Differences of Related Words 59, 3 Valck.; Etymologicum Gudianum 534, 19 De Stef.
1 Αἰσονίδαο in F
2 ἐπι-ον — πάθος in L : -ος — πόθος in P
c. δειδυῖαν: of the verb δείδω the perfect is δείδια, from which the participle by syncope is δειδώς, the feminine δειδυῖα.
754. Fallow land of Ares: the plain ploughed by the bulls. Lm (P)
755. ἔθυιεν: rushed, moved. Hence also θυιάδες, the Bacchae. Lm (P)
6 scholium on I 636a with similar passages.
9 κινεῖται in Lg

756-59a. As when in the halls of the sun: just as a ray of the sun in a house is reflected from water onto a wall, which has just been poured either in a cauldron or in a bucket, and it moves continuously to each side, whirling. L
b. In a pail: in a bucket, which is called βεδοῦριν. Lm (P)
c. With swift eddy: with very swift whirling. Lg (P)
762. 〈Wasting pain〉 consuming: the pain was wearing her down, burning. Homer (I 653): 'to consume the ships with fire'. Lm (P)

764-65a. 〈There most grievous:〉 in which place is the most painful part of the soul, whenever someone is continually possessed by love. He plausibly dwells on the character of one who is drawn by passion but controlled by reason. Lm (P)
15 τόπον in F : τρ-

b. ἐνικίμψωσιν: may fall upon. LgP
767. καταφθίσθαι: that is, by love. Lm (P)
769a. ὀτλησέμεν: she considered enduring the ruin. Lg (P)
b. And εὔκηλον instead of εὐκήλως, that is, quietly. P
772. 〈ἀλκή:〉 escape. Lg
775a. Achaean: instead of Thessalian. Homer (B 684): 'Myrmidons were they called, and Hellenes and Achaeans.' L
b. 〈Before coming to the Achaean land:〉 it is written 'before bringing to the Achaean land'. Lm
28 added in HF
780. 〈Having devised drugs:〉 the word 'to give' is missing. The preposition ἐπί is redundant.
781. What counsel: what deceptive plan of help will there be for me? Lm (P)
785. ἀπαμείρεται: will be deprived. LgP
787. 〈ἵνα οἱ:〉 where for him. Lg
789. 〈μελάθρω:〉 to the beam. Lg
7 scholium on I 486a with similar passages.
791. ἐπιλλίξουσιν: they will mock at. Properly, to close the eyes in mockery. Lm (P)
7 ἐπιλλίξουσιν O. Schneider in Merkel's edition : -ίζουσιν
796. Badly the word οὕς — better through ε, ἑούς — 〈has been used instead of ἐμούς. Or ...〉, so that the speech may be from the women. L
